confirmed.statement: All four reader procedures answer over HTTPS GET on https://www.emuready.com/api/mobile/trpc/<procedure>?input=<percent-encoded JSON> with HTTP/2 200 and content-type application/json; the parser's envelope result.data.json is present for every procedure.

games.batchBySteamAppIds returns success as a JSON boolean true, a results array, and per-row string steamAppId plus matchStrategy exact|not_found; a not-found row still exists with game:null. The parser handles both the game row and the null-game row without exceptions.

The batch endpoint really does return console entries for Windows Steam AppIDs: AppID 400 -> nintendo_switch Portal, 1174180 -> sony_playstation_4 RDR2, 413150 -> nintendo_switch Stardew Valley, 1145360 -> nintendo_switch Hades. The committed microsoft_windows guard is therefore load-bearing on live data; without it console reports would leak into the Windows reader.

Batch matching does not depend on game.metadata.steamAppId: all matched games had metadata null, yet selectGame(matchedBySteamAppId=true) correctly accepts the row's Windows game as the requested AppID's entry.

The games.get title fallback resolves a unique Windows entry when the batch row is missing or console-only, using APPROVED + microsoft_windows + UUID + exact title. Live cases: Portal (AppID 400, batch was Switch) and Grand Theft Auto V (AppID 271590, batch not_found). Portal title search had 9 rows (Windows + Switch); GTA V search had 24 rows across PS3/PS4/PS5/Xbox/Windows.

Some Windows games that exist in EmuReady are not found by the batch AppID lookup: Grand Theft Auto V (AppID 271590, 230 listings) and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (AppID 292030, Windows entry seen in the broad search) both returned matchStrategy not_found. The title fallback is therefore not only for unindexed games; it is needed for real, well-populated entries.

Queries with no EmuReady catalog entry (Team Fortress 2, Half-Life 2: Episode One, Ghostrunner Demo) return games:[] with pagination.total 0. The reader turns that into Page(null, emptyList, ambiguous=false) with no exception.

listings.get returns a listings array plus a pagination object with integer counts and boolean hasNextPage/hasPreviousPage. All 39 sampled rows across 3 games (Half-Life 2 8, Portal 11, GTA V 20) satisfy every parseReport guard: UUID listing id, matching gameId and nested game.id, APPROVED listing status, nested microsoft_windows system, device brand.name + modelName, device soc.name, emulator.name, performance.label, string notes, non-negative int upvoteCount/downvoteCount, ISO createdAt whose first 10 chars are YYYY-MM-DD.

For a game with 230 listings the API returns exactly 20 rows for limit=20 with hasNextPage=true, so the parser's size>LIMIT rejection is not tripped and hasMore is recognized. hasNextPage=false was also observed on smaller games.

listings.byId returns the listing object directly under result.data.json with id, gameId, APPROVED status, nested Windows game and customFieldValues. Across 2 reports, 61 custom-field items each had customFieldDefinition.label as a string and value as a primitive (51 strings, 10 booleans, 0 arrays, 0 nulls), all <= 100 items; the reader's label/value/blank/limit rules yield 23 settings per report.

ids are UUID strings (not integers) on games, listings and custom-field items; steamAppId is a decimal JSON string in batch rows; createdAt is an ISO-8601 string; votes and pagination counts are JSON numbers (integers); hasNextPage is a JSON boolean; metadata is null or an object with igdbId and was never observed carrying steamAppId. These match the parser's JsonPrimitive accessors.
The reader's generated source URL https://www.emuready.com/listings/<report id> and browse URL https://www.emuready.com/listings?search=<title> both returned 200 text/html in a supplementary check.

findings.gap_note: No live payload shape required a change to app/src/main/feature/library/EmuReady.kt. Every sampled shape matched what the committed parser accepts; the guard and fallback decisions behaved as designed against real data. The items below are residual risks that live sampling did not exercise, not observed defects; no code change is recommended without evidence.

residual_risks_not_triggered_live.risk: parseReport throws on the first non-conforming row, so a future PENDING/REJECTED or shape-broken row inside page 1 would blank the whole page instead of skipping that row. All 39 sampled page-1 rows were APPROVED.
residual_risks_not_triggered_live.minimal_fix_if_ever_confirmed: filter rows to the expected shape before mapping, or skip non-APPROVED listings instead of failing the page

residual_risks_not_triggered_live.risk: No live game carried metadata.steamAppId (always null or igdbId-only), so the string-vs-number type could not be confirmed live; the parser's contentOrNull handles both, and existing injected tests cover them.
No live customFieldValues item had an array value (61 primitive items observed), so the array branch of parseDetails remains validated only by injected tests.

The fallback still requires trimmed case-insensitive title equality; a Steam title that differs from EmuReady's by punctuation/localization would miss only when batch lookup also fails. Live fallback examples (Portal, Grand Theft Auto V) matched exactly, and the batch path no longer depends on titles.
residual_risks_not_triggered_live.minimal_fix_if_ever_confirmed: use normalizedTitle equality only after an AppID-confirmed batch row, or fall back to normalized comparison in the title search

residual_risks_not_triggered_live.risk: games.get returned zero results for 'Team Fortress 2', 'Half-Life 2: Episode One' and 'Ghostrunner Demo'; the exact reason (no catalog entry vs search tokenization) cannot be distinguished from one endpoint. Evidence indicates no catalog entry (episode/subtitle probes also empty; broad 'Ghostrunner' search finds the full game).
residual_risks_not_triggered_live.minimal_fix_if_ever_confirmed: none for the reader; a broader search strategy would be an upstream/UX decision

residual_risks_not_triggered_live.risk: All batch/search game rows seen were status APPROVED; a non-APPROVED variant would be filtered by selectGame (safe) but was not sampled live.

limitations: Single host and single observation window (2026-10-21 ~18:07-18:11 UTC). EmuReady data and catalog coverage drift; ids, counts and listing contents in this receipt are snapshots.

No Android app or emulator run was performed (not required by the brief). Compatibility is established by an offline behavioural simulation of the committed parser over raw live payloads, not by executing the app.
Only the four read procedures were sampled; HTTP error bodies, trpc error envelopes, timeouts and cancellation paths were not exercised live.
Only page 1 of three games' listings was sampled; deeper pages (hasPreviousPage) were not fetched.
User-Agent probes used curl only (browser-like, default curl, empty). OkHttp's own 'okhttp/x' default UA was not probed; however the mobile path answered 200 even with no UA header.
Exact earlier 403 requests were not recorded by the prior passes, so 'wrong path/origin gate' is inferred from a controlled probe, not proven.
games.get search semantics (ranking/tokenization) are undocumented, so 'zero results' is evidence about these queries, not proof that a title is absent from EmuReady.
Settings validation covered 2 reports (30 and 31 custom-field items); other reports may have different field subsets or types (e.g. arrays) not seen here.
Raw payloads contain public user-generated content (notes, author identifiers) and are deliberately kept outside the repo; only hashes are committed.
